Your Reel insights show a skip rate: the share of viewers who swiped away in the first 3 seconds. The $1K Club Playbook covers how to read it. Three ways to keep that number down:

deleted.title: If You Can Make It 1: The sandwich (bread, spread, and two ways to stand out)
deleted.hook: If you can make a sandwich, you can make something people pay for. Let me show you how.
deleted.notes:
Mercedes's idea 2026-10-30, the pilot. Her original hook: 'If you can make a sandwich, you can make $1K in the next 30 days.' Changed because the content rules say never promise $1,000 (and no timeline). Other safe options: 'you already know how to start your first $1K' / 'you can build your first $1K product'.

Beats: every sandwich needs bread and spread. Some are only bread and spread: PB&J. A staple, huge appeal, nothing different about it. Unless: (1) you cut it with a cookie cutter, think Uncrustables: the simplest thing, shaped the same way every time, so people recognise it; or (2) artisan ingredients, homemade bread and jam: same big-audience thing, quality you notice. Lesson: you don't need a new idea, you need a recognisable shape or noticeably better quality, done consistently.
Close: make something you love, share it with the world, and go after your next $1K.

Series rule: every episode = one thing people already know how to make + one business lesson, same closing line.
